title: Quentin and the Crown Anew
premise: Cyrus Almeida, a scribe indentured to the Temple of the Ledger in a valley where magic cannot survive, learns that his late mother sold his soul to the Undercourt beneath Mount Vessel to pay her debts. When the old gods stir and begin answering prayers again, their returning power cracks the valley's ancient wards, and Cyrus is chosen—unwillingly—as the one mortal whose unbought soul can carry a petition into the court. Guided by Quentin, a fox-spirited godling of small justices, he descends into a bureaucracy of stolen souls where every bargain has a loophole and every mercy has a price. To free himself, Cyrus must argue his own case before the Crown Anew, expose the court's founding fraud, and choose between reclaiming his soul or spending it to buy freedom for thousands of debt-bound dead.
about_author: Hazel Pemberton is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing legal ledgers from abandoned mountain monasteries, an experience that taught her how much cruelty can hide in neat handwriting. She writes fantasy about ordinary people trapped in extraordinary paperwork, and lives near a river she suspects of remembering things.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Cyrus copies debt ledgers in the Temple of the Ledger, invisible among hundreds of indentured scribes, until a prayer he mutters over a dying colleague is answered for the first time in living memory. Told from Cyrus's POV. The emotional beat is the vertigo of being noticed after a lifetime of careful erasure.

chapters.title: A Fox at the Window
chapters.summary: Quentin, a minor godling of small justices, appears in Cyrus's cell and reveals that the old gods are waking because the valley's wards are failing—and that Cyrus's soul was sold to the Undercourt before his birth. Told from Cyrus's POV. The beat is betrayal: even his mother's love came with fine print.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Owes
chapters.summary: Cyrus searches the temple archives for his mother's contract and finds the High Scribe burning records to hide the temple's own complicity in soul-trading. He steals the page naming him. Told from Cyrus's POV with an interlude from the High Scribe. The beat is righteous anger hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Leaving the Wards
chapters.summary: Cyrus flees the valley through the ward-stones as temple hunters pursue him; crossing the boundary, magic floods back into the world and Quentin takes true form. Told from Cyrus's POV. The beat is terror transforming into exhilaration—the first breath of a self he never owned.

chapters.title: The Road of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Traveling toward Mount Vessel, Cyrus and Quentin settle tiny injustices along the way—a cheated widow, a bound spirit—and gather followers among the forgotten. Told alternately from Cyrus's POV and a widow named Maren's. The beat is belonging found among strangers who were also erased.

chapters.title: The Gate of Names
chapters.summary: At the mountain's gate, a customs-house of souls, Cyrus must surrender his name to enter; Quentin warns that names once given to the court are never returned intact. Told from Cyrus's POV. The beat is sacrifice—he gives up 'Cyrus Almeida' and walks in as no one at all.

chapters.title: Beneath, the Bureaucracy
chapters.summary: In the Undercourt, Cyrus witnesses the machinery of soul-debt: endless queues, forged signatures, and his mother's original contract, which reveals she was deceived too. Told from Cyrus's POV. The beat is grief transmuted into understanding—she was a victim, not a traitor.

chapters.title: The Petition
chapters.summary: Cyrus files a formal petition challenging the court's right to collect on contracts signed under false pretense, while Quentin rallies the small gods to jam the court's procedures. Told from Cyrus's POV with fragments of the Crown's cold perspective. The beat is desperate courage as the case hangs by a technicality.

chapters.title: Before the Crown Anew
chapters.summary: At trial, Cyrus exposes the court's founding fraud—that its authority rests on a soul it never legally purchased—and the Crown offers him a choice: take back his soul alone, or void every contract and unmake the court. Told from Cyrus's POV. The beat is the climax: justice offered as a personal prize versus justice given away.

chapters.title: Everything Unbought
chapters.summary: Cyrus spends his claim to free all debt-bound souls; the Undercourt dissolves, the dead go home, and he returns to the valley nameless but free, where Quentin teaches him to write new covenants instead of debts. Told from Cyrus's POV with a closing passage from Quentin's. The beat is quiet resolution: identity rebuilt not from what he owns, but what he gave.
